newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia trade deficit surges to 2.8 bln rgt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia trade deficit surges to 2.8 bln rgt.

text.p: Big purchases of ships and planes propelled Malaysia's trade deficit to 2.8 billion ringgit in June against a surplus of 156.2 million in May, the Statistics Department said on Monday.
Exports in June totalled 16.5 billion ringgit against imports of 19.3 billion, the department said.

The department said the deficit in June was caused by the purchase of ships and tankers, including a liquefied natural gas carrier, and commercial aircraft, amounting to 2.2 billion ringgit or 11.4 percent of total imports.
In the first six months of this year, Malaysia posted a deficit of 2.7 billion ringgit against a deficit of 687.8 million in the same period last year.
Imports in the six months period were at 101.1 billion ringgit, higher by 3.9 billion ringgit or an increase of four percent compared with the 97.2 billion registered in the same period last year.
Exports, on the other hand, rose by 1.8 billion ringgit or 1.9 percent, to 98.4 billion from 96.6 billion in the first six months of 1996.
Increased imports in transport equipment and office data processing equipment of 1.4 billion and 1.1 billion respectively partly contributed to the trade deficit during the first half of 1997.

The department said thermionic valves and tubes, photocells and parts continued to be the country's largest export earner, netting receipts amounting to 18.1 billion and accounting for 18.4 percent of the total export earnings.
Major reductions in export earnings were recorded for rubber (364.1 million ringgit or 20.2 percent), crude petroleum (263.5 million or 7.2 percent), and sawn timber (155.5 million or 10.2 percent).

The department said the import of intermediate goods constituted the largest proportion of goods imported, accounting for 65.7 billion, or 64.9 percent of total imports while capital goods were valued at 21 billion ringgit, accounting for 20.8 percent of total imports.
